PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS.name: PUBG
PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS.headline: PUBG's daily peak fell 47% across the window. 14-day forecasts were off by 8% on average, and the 80% band held 68% of the time.

bullets.label: Trend
bullets.text: Daily peak averaged 1.60M in the first four weeks and 841K in the last four (-47%).

bullets.label: Forecast accuracy
bullets.text: Out of sample, 14-day forecasts were off by 7.7% on average. The 'same weekday last week' baseline was off by 9.9%. That beats the baseline by 23%.

bullets.label: Can the bands be trusted?
bullets.text: The 80% band contained the real value 68% of the time and the 95% band 79%, over 115 scored days. The band was too narrow, which usually means the series became more volatile than the period used to calibrate it. I would recalibrate on a rolling window and monitor coverage weekly.

bullets.label: Holdout check
bullets.text: Forecasting from Feb 27, day 14 (Mar 13) came out at 768K (80% band 696K to 849K). The actual value was 782K, inside the band.

bullets.label: Anomalies
bullets.text: 3 events flagged: 3 title-specific, 0 platform-wide, 0 sitting next to a data gap. Only the title-specific ones are candidates for a product explanation.

bullets.label: Data caveat
bullets.text: 12 of 306 days were interpolated for model fitting and were never scored. Usable snapshot coverage after cleaning is 97.17%.

bullets.label: What the integrity check was worth
bullets.text: Run the identical method on the data WITHOUT removing frozen snapshots and the forecast error is 17.7% instead of 7.7%, and the 80% band holds 61% of the time instead of 68%. A few stretches of stale values made a sound model look broken.

next_steps: Join this with a live-ops calendar (patches, events, sales) so title-specific spikes get a cause, not just a flag.
Segment by platform, region and player tenure, which Steam's public counts cannot provide.
Track forecast error and interval coverage weekly, and recalibrate automatically when coverage drifts.
Turn the weekly report into a scheduled job that writes the note and flags only what changed.
